law: ONE function -> ONE current authority class. This file is generated from tools/authority_lib.py#AUTHORITY_SURFACE and is the single machine-readable classification authority. Where any other current artifact speaks about one of these functions, it must agree with this file, and any slot whose semantics are 'this function authorizes X' must name a function classified authorizing. Authority selection is itself an authorizing decision (Codex v1.15 V115-B1).

classes.authorizing: may decide an authority question. Requires governed provenance (a GovernedEvidenceSet minted by load_governed_evidence_set) wherever it consumes evidence.
classes.diagnostic_non_authorizing: the same SEMANTIC derivation over a bare evidence set. No governed provenance, no location receipt. For fixtures, in-memory evidence and diagnosis. Its result may look like a readiness or eligibility answer and is never authority.
classes.provisional_until_m3_non_authorizing: composed transaction/commit validation over a bare evidence set. Every stage law is identical to the authorizing pair, but without governed provenance the result is not write authority.
classes.internal_non_authorizing: a helper composed by the authority; never a public decision point.

slot_discovery_law.definition: Every concrete occurrence of every canonical authority_lib function class is in scope, in JSON keys and values and logical Markdown units. Metadata records are declarations about occurrences, not recursively scanned occurrences. Source-bound declarations cannot suppress contradictory normative predicates.
slot_discovery_law.clause_law: A claim is read ONLY from the clause containing the reference. Clauses break at '.', ';', ':', ',' and newline, at parenthesis depth zero, and only where the delimiter is followed by whitespace or the end of the text - so an argument list, a dotted module path and a version number stay intact while ordinary punctuation ends a clause. Wrapped markdown prose is rejoined into logical lines first, so where a line happens to wrap cannot change a classification.
slot_discovery_law.negation_law: Negation is LOCAL, never a phrase search. 'X is no longer authoritative; Y is authoritative' classifies X non-authorizing and Y authorizing, because each clause is read separately. No bare negation appears in any token list: the v1.16 scanner exempted any sentence containing the phrase 'no longer', and in the TOCTOU law that phrase modified 'the bundle's binding no longer resolves' - an unrelated clause - which suppressed a real diagnostic-name violation (V116-B1).
signal_precedence: Schema-defined class keys and registered superseded rows establish structural role.
Collect own-clause per-reference predicates independently. Reject a conflicting metadata declaration.
Source-bound structured declaration resolves otherwise ambiguous prose; then predicate-local fallback. Unresolved current references fail closed.
slot_discovery_law.module_awareness: A same-named function in another module is a DIFFERENT symbol: evidence_authoring.derive_attachment_state is the AUTHORIZING authoring wrapper, not the diagnostic authority_lib core function, and is recorded as a foreign-module symbol rather than judged against the authority_lib class map.

laws.R1: A current demoted function reference requires its own non-authorizing declaration or registered historical context; neither may contradict a current authority predicate.
laws.R2: every clause that designates authority names a function whose canonical class is authorizing

slot_discovery_law.artifact_scope: derived from AUTHORITY-PRECEDENCE.json: status STILL_ACTIVE and role in (NORMATIVE_AUTHORITY, CORRECTION_RECORD). Never a filename pattern. GENERATED_EVIDENCE (the validation report and the generated inventory) reports what the suite checked and quotes its own check names, so it is out of scope by published role; HISTORICAL_INPUT is out of scope by status.
slot_discovery_law.generator: tools/authority_slots.py, used by both this build and validate_v1_19.py
slot_discovery_law.ambiguity_law: AMBIGUOUS_CURRENT_REFERENCE fails validation; current decision-function MENTION is allowed only for an explicitly foreign module symbol.
slot_discovery_law.reference_universe: All functions in the canonical authorizing, diagnostic, provisional and internal class arrays; values and JSON keys (location suffix .@key).
slot_discovery_law.history_law: Registered superseded statement rows use their frozen effective version in both JSON and Markdown. A free-text historical annotation cannot erase a current authority predicate.
slot_discovery_law.non_authorizing_occurrences: DIAGNOSTIC_DECLARATION records a non-authorizing occurrence, including internal helper descriptions and data identifiers sharing function names. It does not demote the canonical function class. An independently detected authority predicate cannot be suppressed by that declaration.

runtime_lookup_law: NO authorizing runtime code resolves a function by name from any artifact. Functions are bound statically by Python import; there is no getattr/eval/dispatch-table lookup keyed on an artifact string anywhere in the authority. A stale artifact can therefore mislead a HUMAN or an external consumer - which is why this file exists and why the validator compares every current artifact against it - but it cannot make the authority itself call a diagnostic function.

bound_fields.source: caller-supplied session id, validated by session_id_errors and compared with both authority files' own claims
DERIVED: canonical_document_path(session_id) from the frozen governed root
DERIVED: canonical_workflow_path(session_id) from the frozen governed root (v1.15 V114-B4)
FROZEN CONSTANT: GOVERNED_ATTACHMENT_ROOT; no caller input participates
FROZEN CONSTANT: AUTHORITY_VERSION of this bundle
active authority: active['manifest_sha256'] of the reviewed manifest
sha256 of the exact EVIDENCE-SET.json bytes read no-follow from the canonical path
sha256 of the exact WORKFLOW.json bytes read no-follow from the canonical path (v1.15 V114-B4)
evidence_snapshot_digest(parse of those exact document bytes) under vidtoolz.resolveEvidenceSetSnapshot.v1 (v1.15 V114-B1)
CONSTANT True: the receipt is only ever computed after location_errors() returned empty; it is not a caller claim

receipt_binding.digest_law: sha256(utf8(domain) + 0x0A + canonical_bytes(object of exactly these fields))
receipt_binding.parity_law: RUNTIME_BOUND_FIELDS == PUBLISHED_BOUND_FIELDS exactly, in both directions and in order; an omitted field or a claimed field the runtime does not bind is a validation failure
